newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD calls for government measures on NTT.
newsitem.headline: KDD calls for government measures on NTT.

text.p: KDD, an international call carrier, worried about telecom giant NTT's planned debut in the international call market, called on the government on Friday to take steps to rein in the domestic powerhouse.

Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co requested that Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's unit to be set up to handle international calls be fully independent of the parent company in accounting, personnel, marketing and other areas.
"NTT's parent company has a bottleneck monopoly (in regional networks)," KDD said in a statement.
"The new unit should stand on equal grounds with other long-distance and international carriers," it said.
NTT last week applied for government approval of a wholly-owned subsidiary to start international call services.
The planned unit, NTT Worldwide Telecommunications Corp, is expected to begin services to corporate clients in the autumn.
Another international carrier, International Telecom Japan Inc, also made the requests similar to KDD's to the government on Friday.
